correctness.rationale: Every primitive two-cycle alternates (u,v,u),(v,u,v); subtracting orbit equations forces u+v=b-1, with discriminant 4(a-a_birth), giving existence/unique unoriented cycle iff a>a_birth. Monodromy J(u)J(v) characteristic p(lambda)=lambda^3+2(b-1)lambda^2+4[b(b-1)-a]lambda-b^2, so p(1)=-4(a-a_birth)<0 gives a real root>1. The characteristic polynomial factors at birth and at a_flip=(5b^2-6b+3)/4; p(-1)=4(a-a_flip). Nonreal unit pair would require other root b^2 and a_pair-a_birth=b(b+2)(b^2-1)/4<0, impossible in existence domain. At flip -1 is simple and crosses outward, while other roots are >1 and in (-1,0). Thus unstable index exactly 1 then 2. Actual Sympy verification source read and direct algebra reconstructed; numeric tests are not proof of unrestricted b. No four-cycle bifurcation inferred.
